_comment: Trigger rules. DETECTION is SQL (deterministic, cheap, auditable). The LLM only comes in AFTER a rule fires. Each row returned by the SQL = one trigger; the columns become {parameters} in the objective.

rules.description: Branch with at least 30% of ratings <= 2 in the last 7 days (minimum 15 ratings)
rules.detect_sql: SELECT r.branch_city || ' ' || r.branch_type AS branch, r.branch_city AS city, r.branch_type AS branch_type, COUNT(*) AS n_ratings, ROUND(AVG(rr.score <= 2) * 100, 1) AS pct_low, (SELECT topic FROM rental_ratings x JOIN rentals y USING(rental_id) WHERE y.branch_city = r.branch_city AND y.branch_type = r.branch_type AND x.score <= 2 AND julianday('2026-10-19') - julianday(x.rated_at) <= 7 GROUP BY topic ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1) AS top_topic FROM rental_ratings rr JOIN rentals r USING (rental_id) WHERE julianday('2026-10-19') - julianday(rr.rated_at) <= 7 GROUP BY r.branch_city, r.branch_type HAVING COUNT(*) >= 15 AND AVG(rr.score <= 2) >= 0.30

actions.message: Low-rating spike at {branch}: {pct_low}% of {n_ratings} ratings (main topic: {top_topic}).

actions.objective: Service-recovery campaign: customers who rated a rental at the {city} ({branch_type}) branch <= 2 in the last 7 days. The main complaint topic is '{top_topic}'. Goal: apologise without an aggressive discount and win back trust for a next rental.

rules.description: At least 1500 first-rental customers who returned the car 30-180 days ago (pool big enough for an A/B test)
rules.detect_sql: SELECT pool, n FROM (SELECT 'first_rental_30_180d' AS pool, COUNT(*) AS n FROM (SELECT customer_id FROM rentals GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) = 1 AND julianday('2026-10-19') - julianday(MAX(return_date)) BETWEEN 30 AND 180)) WHERE n >= 1500

actions.objective: Turn first-rental customers into a second rental. Focus on people who returned the car 1 to 3 months ago; we also want to push app adoption.
